# **Floppy 80 (M1) v2 User Guide**

# **Configuration**

An SD Card (FAT formatted) is required to contain the disk images, and configuration. The card must be an SDHC or SDXC card (larger than 2 GB). Older standard capacity SD cards, up to and including 2 GB, are not supported by the default firmware. A firmware built with the LEGACY SD card library option (see BUILDING.md) does support them.

Configuration of the Floppy80-M1 is performed with the placement of files on the SD-Card inserted in its card reader. Files are placed in the Root folder (unless noted), subfolders are not generally supported. The files are as follows:

## **system.cfg**

This file contains global configuration settings. The file and settings are optional, and all have meaningful defaults. The settings are:

* MEM \- Used to enable / disable 32KB RAM; 1 \= enabled (default); 0 \= disabled  
* LMEM \- Used to enable / disable 16KB of lower memory RAM; 1 \= enabled; 0 \= disabled (default)  
* SDKHZ \- SD card SPI clock in kHz, e.g. SDKHZ=12500. The card is always mounted and system.cfg read at the firmware's boot speed (5000 by default); the clock is then changed to this value. Accepted range is 1000 to 25000\. Not all cards work at higher speeds (a card that is too slow for the setting can make the Floppy80 lock up), so increase it in steps, e.g. 8333, 10000, 12500, and test with your card. If it is missing, the boot speed is kept  
* L3RAM \- Used to enable / disable 1KB of RAM at 3000h-33FFh; 1 \= enabled; 0 \= disabled (default)  
* L3RAMF \- Name of a file (in the root folder) used to fill the L3RAM area at power on, e.g. L3RAMF=BOOT3000.BIN. The file is a raw binary image loaded at 3000h, up to 1024 bytes. If it is shorter, the rest of the area is zero. It is loaded each time the Floppy80 starts or is reset (before the Z80 runs), so it replaces whatever the Z80 had written there. It only has an effect when L3RAM=1. If the file is missing the area is left as zeros  
* VHD \- Used to enable / disable Hard Disk; 1 \= enabled (default); 0 \= disabled  
* WAIT \- Used to enable / disable wait states 1 \= enabled; 0 \= disabled (default)

E.g.

MEM=1  
VHD=0  
WAIT=0  
SDKHZ=6250  
L3RAM=1  
L3RAMF=test.rom

Wait states are used to slow the Z80 CPU, to get it to wait for all floppy disk controller actions to complete before continuing. Typically, wait states should not be required.

**A Note on Wait States:** Wait states slow down the Z80 CPU to ensure it waits for the floppy disk controller emulation to complete. While generally unnecessary for standard systems, they can help with overclocked CPUs where the processor outpaces the emulation. Note that wait states are known to disrupt critical, tightly timed native operations like formatting a physical floppy disk.

## **Option ROM**

The two parameters L3RAM and L3RAMF can be used to load a file into unused address space at 3000H (12288 dec), it can be a maximum of 1024 bytes and was added to provide a way of potentially testing things like boot roms etc. The sd card has the source code for a very simple example in the folder testrom. It compiles at 3000h and just calls CLS and CHAR out routines to display "Hello World\!". it's loaded by default with the system.cfg provided. You can call it from basic, to test it:

Type

SYSTEM  
\*  
Use  
/12288

## **boot.cfg**

Specify the default INI file to load at reset of the Floppy80. When the floppy 80 boots or is reset it reads the contents of the boot.cfg to determine the default configuration INI file.

This file contains (ONLY) the name of the current INI file being used e.g.

E.G.

LD531.INI

## **INI files**

Specifies the disk images and options after reset. Options:

* Drive0 \- specified the image to load for drive :0  
* Drive1 \- specified the image to load for drive :1  
* Drive2 \- specified the image to load for drive :2  
* HD0 \- specifies the image to load for the first hard drive  
* HD1 \- specifies the image to load for the second hard drive  
* Doubler \- 1 \= doubler is enabled; 0 \= doubler is disabled;

E.G

Drive0=LD531-0.dmk  
Drive1=LD531-1.dmk  
Drive2=LD531-2.dmk  
HD0=hard0.hdv  
Doubler=1

## **DMK files**

Virtual floppy disk images with a specific file format that allows them to be generated and used with a number of existing programs and simulators.

## **Virtual Hard Drive Images**

Virtual hard drive images with a specific file format. They are the same format as is used by TRS80-GP. See the section below for an example of creating your own.

## **/FMT folder**

A folder which can contain blank floppy images, these are not mountable. Instead, they used by the FDC FMT command. See FDC FOR section below.

# **Operation**

The Floppy80 should be powered on before the Main computer is powered. Power is provided by the USB port on the Pi Pico microcontroller.

The Floppy-80 has an LED which shows disk activity.

## **Startup**

When Floppy80 first starts it uses boot.cfg to load the default disk images.

# **FDC Utility**

The FDC command-line program allows you to interact with the Floppy 80 directly from inside the TRS-80 operating system. Versions are available for CP/M (Lifeboat and FMG) as well as most major TRSDOS-based environments.

> * FDC STA — Displays the current system status and lists the contents of the active boot INI file.  
> * FDC DIR \[filter\] — Lists files in the SD card's root folder. Adding an optional text filter narrows down the results.  
> * FDC INI \[filename.ini\] — Switches the system to a new INI profile. If you omit the filename, a selectable menu of available INI files will appear, and your choice will be written to boot.cfg file.  
> * FDC DMK \[filename.dmk\] \[0/1/2\] — Mounts a specific floppy image to drive :0, :1, or :2. Running FDC DMK without arguments opens an interactive selection menu.  
  * *Example:* FDC DMK LDOS-DATA.DMK 2 mounts that file to drive :2.  
> * FDC FOR — An emergency backup formatting utility. It lets you select a blank template from the /FMT folder to overwrite and clear a currently mounted drive image if native OS formatting fails.  
> * FDC IMP \[filename.ext\] :n — Imports a raw file from the root of the SD card directly into virtual floppy drive n.  
> * You can also use tools like trs80tools, to import and export files from the disk image files.

## **Operating System Compatibility**

The following matrix details how various TRS-80 Model I operating systems interact with the Floppy 80 emulation layer.

| Operating System | Native Formatting | Backup Utility | Notes / Special Requirements   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CP/M 1.4.1 (Lifeboat)** | Works | Works | Stable |
| **CP/M 1.5 (FMG)** | Works | Works | Stable |
| **Double DOS 4.2.4** | Works | Works | Stable |
| **DOS Plus 3.50** | Works | Conditional | Requires a double-sided .dmk template to format. BACKUP requires Doubler=0. |
| **LDOS 5.3.1** | Conditional | Works | Currently supports single-density only. Requires a system reboot after formatting a drive. |
| **MultiDOS 4.01** | Works | Conditional | BACKUP requires Doubler=0. |
| **NEWDOS 3.0 / 80 V2.0** | Works | Works | Stable |
| **TRSDOS 2.3** | Works | Works | Stable |
| **UltraDOS 4.2.0** | Works | Works | Stable |
| **VTDOS 3.0.0** | Works | Issue | BACKUP encounters "Different Pack IDs" warning. |
| **VTDOS 4.0.1** | Works | Conditional | BACKUP requires Doubler=0. |

## **Advanced use Debugging & Serial Interface**

The Firmware provides a debugging interface for logging and diagnosing issues. In normal use you do not need to use any of these features, it’s in this document as reference.. To use this you need to dismantle the unit and connect to the USB header on the PICO. D**o not power the unit from both external 5v and the USB, only use USB power.**

While running the Floppy 80 provides a Command Line interface via serial over the USB port on the Pi PICO. Simply connect a USB can to a host computer and connect a Serial Communications program to the serial port.

While the port may appear differently on different operating systems on a Mac it appears something like dev/cu.usbmodem000000. The port is not a true serial port and has no explicit Baud Rate, etc.

Pressing enter should display a help menu explaining the basic commands. A few of the commands have matching FDC commands.

| `COMMAND` | `FDC` | `DESCRIPTION` |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| boot f | FDC INI | Set INI file (f) to use for boot |
| disks |  | Display information about mounted disks |
| dir f | FDC DIR | Display a Directory (optional filter) |
| dump n |  | Dump Drive (n) contents |
| hdc |  | Create a Virtual Hard Disk |
| help |  | Display CLI Help screen |
| logon |  | Enable FDC Debug Output |
| logoff |  | Disable FDC Debug Output |
| status | FDC STA | Display Status |

Some of the more important commands are described below.

## **Advanced: Setting Up a Virtual Hard Disk (Beta)**

This brief walk through uses LDOS as an example.

### **Prerequisites**

> 1. A working, bootable Drive 0 floppy image containing the standard **RSHARD** drivers (e.g., RSHARD5 for LDOS). These drivers can be found in the download section of Tim Mann's TRS-80 archive.  
> 2. A blank .hdv hard disk image. The most reliable way to generate a fresh image container is using an emulator like **trs80gp**.

### **Hard Disk Partitioning**

Because traditional standard configurations (like 309 tracks, 4 heads) are to large to be supported as a single drive on a trs80, you should subdivide  the drive into smaller sizes for example 4-partitions split into **38 cylinders per partition**. It works best to disregard the last track, If you try to push the last partition to 39 cylinders, the LDOS formatter will drop the drive down to a 35-track default layout. Some other combinations also cause this issue, I think it’s a bug in the LDOS drivers.

Follow these configuration steps carefully inside your emulator before copying the file over to your physical Floppy 80 hardware:

> 1. **Initialize the Driver for Partition 1 (Drive :4)**  
>    Boot your LDOS 5.3.1 image in the emulator. Execute the driver initialization command and provide the geometry values below when prompted:

> 2. `SYSTEM (DRIVE=4,DISABLE,DRIVER="RSHARD5")`  
>    `Enter drive address <1-2> and F/R: 1F`  
>    `Enter the STEP RATE: [Press Enter for default]`  
>    `Enter the physical TRACKS per surface: 153`  
>    `Enter the total number of HEADS: 8`  
>    `Enter partition's number of heads: 8`  
>    `Enter partition's number of cylinders: 38`  
>        

> **Initialize Partition 2 (Drive :5)**  
> Bind the second virtual drive slice using the remaining available head allocation:

> `SYSTEM (DRIVE=5,DISABLE,DRIVER="RSHARD5")`  
> `Enter partition's number of heads: 8`  
> `Enter partition's number of cylinders: 38`  
>     

> 3. **Initialize Partition 3 (Drive :6)**  
>    Bind the third virtual drive slice:

>   
> `SYSTEM (DRIVE=6,DISABLE,DRIVER="RSHARD5")`  
> `Enter drive address <1-2> and F/R: 1F`  
> `Enter partition's number of heads: 8`  
> `Enter partition's number of cylinders: 38`  
>     

> 4. **Initialize Partition 4 (Drive :7)**  
>    Bind the final virtual partition slice:

> `SYSTEM (DRIVE=7,DISABLE,DRIVER="RSHARD5")`  
> `Enter drive address <1-2> and F/R: 1F`  
> `Enter partition's number of heads: 8`  
> `Enter partition's number of cylinders: 38`  
>     

> 5. **Format the New Partitions**  
>    Run the Western Digital high-level formatter utility on each allocated drive. Repeat this process for drives :5, :6, and :7.  
>    `RSFORM5 :4`  
>    `Disk Pack name? HD04`  
>    `Master password? PASSWORD`  
>    `Are you sure you want to format it <Y,N>? Y`  
>    `Lock out track manually <Y/N>? N`

> `Repeat for each partition 4,5,6,7`  
>     

> 6. **Commit Configuration via Sysgen**

> Save your newly assigned drive mappings so they survive system restarts by running:  
> `SYSTEM (SYSGEN)`  
>     

### **Copy to the Floppy 80**

Once configured via the emulator, move your files onto the physical SD card and ensure your configuration parameters match the layout below:

**Create an INI profile (e.g., ldosboothd.ini):**  
`Drive0=ldosboot2s.dmk`  
`HD0=ldosboothd.hdv`

Ensure that VHD=1 is specified within your global system.cfg, and check that your boot.cfg points directly to your newly created hard disk .ini profile. Once booted, typing FREE or DEVICES at the LDOS prompt will verify your active virtual hard disk sub-systems.

### **Dump Drive Contents**

`dump n` \- where n is the drive number. Display a complete sector-by-sector list of the chosen (mounted) disk to the console.

### **Logon / Logoff**

Enables or disables the output to the console of FDC debugging activity information.
